newsitem.title: USA: Florida Catholic diocese hit by priest scandals.
newsitem.headline: Florida Catholic diocese hit by priest scandals.

text.p: A Roman Catholic priest in Florida was forced to resign over allegations of sexual misconduct, the third sex-related scandal to hit the diocese in a week, church officials said on Thursday.

The Diocese announced earlier this week that Father William Lau, former pastor of the Blessed Trinity Catholic Church in St. Petersburg, resigned in May when an adult complained of an incident that occurred "many years" ago.
The St. Petersburg Times reported the incident involved sexual misconduct with a minor, but added that the church refused to say whether the minor was a boy or a girl.
Lau, 46, has entered an institute in Washington for "assessment and rehabilitation therapy," the diocese said.
On Monday, the Diocese said that Rev. Patrick Clarke, 52, of the Espiritu Santo Catholic Church in Safety Harbour, had been suspended because of a secret marriage in 1981.
But church officials were quick to assure parishioners that the sacraments he had administered during those years, including marriages and baptisms, were valid under church law.
The next day, the Diocese announced the resignation of Father Simeon Gardner, pastor of St. Mary's Church in Lutz.

Gardner, 69, had been diverting church money -- about $220,000 according to a preliminary audit -- for three years to a man with whom he had "improper and impermissible sexual conduct," the diocese said in a statement.

Robert Lynch, Bishop of the Diocese, told a news conference that he was sorry for the priests, their parishioners and "for all priests who ... will once again wonder if they too will be painted with the brush of infidelity to promise and absence of honesty and integrity."
